title: Up and down buttonhole stitch
subtitle: Alternating upward and downward bars that produce a knotted-edge border
excerpt: Up and down buttonhole stitch alternates the direction of every bar: one bar points toward the outer edge, the next points back toward the inner line. The alternating motion produces a double-knotted cord at both the inner and outer edges, making a decorative border that is more substantial than plain buttonhole stitch.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), buttonhole stitch variations. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), buttonhole stitch entry.

content.text: Up and down buttonhole stitch pairs each standard downward buttonhole bar with a reversed upward bar placed immediately beside it. The downward bar loops at the outer edge; the upward bar loops at the inner line. Together they produce a knotted cord at both edges of the row. The motion is slightly more complex than plain buttonhole stitch but the stitch moves at a similar pace once the pairing rhythm is established.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 or 3 strands; pearl cotton no. 8 for a firm knotted cord

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Evenweave linen or firm cotton; mark two parallel guide lines before starting

content.text: Mark an inner and an outer guide line the desired bar height apart. Fasten the thread on the back. Bring the needle up at point (A) on the inner line.

Work a standard downward buttonhole bar: insert the needle at point (B) on the outer line, one bar-width to the right. Bring the tip up at (C) on the inner line directly above (B). Pass the thread under the needle and pull through. The loop locks at the outer edge.

Now work the upward bar: insert the needle at point (D) on the inner line, one bar-width to the right of (C). Bring the tip up at point (E) on the outer line directly below (D). Pass the thread under the needle tip from right to left before pulling through. The loop locks at the inner edge.
Continue across the row, alternating a downward bar (looping at the outer edge) with an upward bar (looping at the inner edge). Keep the spacing between bars even.
At the end of the row, take the thread to the back just past the last bar to secure the edge cord.

attrs.heading: When up and down buttonhole stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: Loops all land on the same edge rather than alternating
items.cause: The thread direction for the upward bar is not reversed before pulling through.
items.fix: For the upward bar, pass the thread under the needle from right to left, the opposite direction from the downward bar.

items.symptom: The row drifts above or below the guide lines
items.cause: Bar insertion points are not kept on the guide lines consistently.
items.fix: Check each new insertion point against the guide lines before placing the needle.

items.symptom: Knots look larger on one edge than the other
items.cause: Pull tension differs between upward and downward bars.
items.fix: Draw both types of bar through with the same firmness and use the same thread length each time.
